adjudication.evidence: Original N/E/U show a sustained offset beginning ~522 (sharp drop in all axes), followed by a gradual return starting ~570–572. P1 (522–570) captures the onset but ends before the return begins; P2 (571) and P3 (572–573) are isolated single-day spikes inconsistent with a smooth return—E and U residuals after 570 show continuous recovery, not discrete jumps. Hypotheses P1–P3 subtracting onset offsets fail to flatten residuals across the return interval; only a single temporary platform spanning ~522 to ~574 (encompassing the full offset+recovery) yields flat residuals. No independent permanent step is evident within this interval; motion is smooth post-570. Thus, P1/P2/P3 are fragmented and non-genuine; replace with empty set pending refined boundary estimation.
